questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 17 + 10 × 5 ÷ 9 + 18 = 53
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

17 + 10 × 5 ÷ 9 + 18 = 53
questions.solution:
(4) × and ÷

⇒ 17 + 10 × 5 ÷ 9 + 18 = 53

After interchanging the signs:

⇒ 17 + 10 ÷ 5 × 9 + 18 = 53

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 17 + 2 × 9 + 18 = 53

⇒ 17 + 18 + 18 = 53

⇒ 53 = 53

questions.question: Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All peacocks are pigeons. Some pigeons are pinks. Some pinks are birds. Conclusions: (I) Some pinks are peacocks. (II) Some birds are pigeons. (III) Some peacocks are birds.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements.

Statements:

All peacocks are pigeons.

Some pigeons are pinks.

Some pinks are birds.

Conclusions:

(I) Some pinks are peacocks.

(II) Some birds are pigeons.

(III) Some peacocks are birds.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows
options.html: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows

questions.solution:
(I) Some pinks are peacocks. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between pinks and peacocks. Hence, false)

(II) Some birds are pigeons. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between birds and pigeons. Hence, false)

(III) Some peacocks are birds. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between birds and peacocks. Hence, false)

Hence, 'None of the conclusion follow' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Pointing to a woman, Param(a man) said, "She is the mother-in-law of the mother-in-law of the daughter-in-law of my father." How is Param related to the woman?
questions.questionHtml: Pointing to a woman, Param(a man) said, "She is the mother-in-law of the mother-in-law of the daughter-in-law of my father." How is Param related to the woman?
questions.solution:
The mother-in-law of the daughter-in-law of my father is my mother.

Mother-in-law of my mother is my paternal grandmother.

Therefore, Param is grandson of the woman.

Hence, 'Grandson' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All birds are ducks. Some ducks are crows. All crows are parrots. Conclusions: I. Some parrots are birds. II. Some parrots are ducks. III. Some crows are birds. IV. All parrots are birds.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All birds are ducks.

Some ducks are crows.

All crows are parrots.

Conclusions:

I. Some parrots are birds.

II. Some parrots are ducks.

III. Some crows are birds.

IV. All parrots are birds.

options.text: Only conclusions I and IV follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and IV follow

options.text: Only conclusions I, II and IV follow
options.html: Only conclusions I, II and IV follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
I. Some parrots are birds. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between parrots and birds. Hence, false)

II. Some parrots are ducks. → Follows (As, Some ducks are crows and All crows are parrots)

III. Some crows are birds. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between crows and birds. Hence, false)

IV. All parrots are birds. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between parrots and birds. Hence, false)

Hence, ‘Only conclusion II follows’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 20 are girls. The average weight of the boys in the class is 40 kg, while that of all the girls is 35 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of the entire class (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 60 students, 20 are girls. The average weight of the boys in the class is 40 kg, while that of all the girls is 35 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of the entire class (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
Let the average weight (in kg) of the entire class be x.

Sum of weight of all boys = 40 × 40 = 1600

Sum of weight of all girls = 20 × 35 = 700

The sum of weight of all classes = 60x

⇒ 60x = 1600 + 700 ⇒ 60x = 2300 ⇒ x = 38.33 kg

questions.question: If Cosec θ + Cot θ = m, find the value of \(\rm\frac{m^{2}−1}{m^{2}+1}\) .
questions.questionHtml: If Cosec θ + Cot θ = m, find the value of \(\rm\frac{m^{2}−1}{m^{2}+1}\).
questions.solution:
cosec θ + cot θ = m      ---- (1)

⇒ (cosec θ - cot θ)(cosec θ + cot θ) = 1 ⇒ (cosec θ - cot θ) =1/m      ---- (2)

2cosecθ = m + 1/m ⇒ cosecθ = (m2 + 1)/2m  ...(3)

cotθ = (m2 - 1)/2m   ...(4)

⇒ \(\rm\frac{m^{2}−1}{m^{2}+1}\)

Putting eq. (3) and (4) in above expression:

⇒ 2mcotθ/2mcosecθ  ⇒ cotθ/cosecθ ⇒ cosθ

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio \(\frac{4}{5}:\frac{5}{6}:\frac{9}{10}\) . The difference between the smallest and the greatest numbers is 12. Find the number which is NEITHER the smallest NOR the greatest.
questions.questionHtml: Three numbers are in the ratio \(\frac{4}{5}:\frac{5}{6}:\frac{9}{10}\). The difference between the smallest and the greatest numbers is 12. Find the number which is NEITHER the smallest NOR the greatest.
questions.solution:
LCM of 5, 6 and 10 is 30.

4/5 ×  30 = 24, 5/6 ×  30 = 25 and 9/10 ×  30 = 27

⇒ A ∶ B ∶ C = 24x ∶ 25x ∶ 27x

⇒ 27x - 24x = 12 ⇒ 3x = 12 ⇒ x = 4

First number = 24x = 24 × 4 = 96; Second number = 25x = 25 × 4 = 100; Third number = 27x = 27 × 4 = 108

100 is neither the smallest nor greatest.

questions.question: The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 15 cm and 13 cm, whose centres are 14 cm apart, is:
questions.questionHtml: The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 15 cm and 13 cm, whose centres are 14 cm apart, is:
questions.solution:
AM = BM = AB/2 

⇒ AM2 = 132 - x2  ...(1)  

BM2 = 152 - (14 - x)2  ...(2)

Equating both the equations:

⇒ 152 - (14 - x)2 = 132 - x2 ⇒ 225 - 196 - x2 + 28x = 169 - x2 ⇒ 28x = 140 ⇒ x = 5

⇒ AM2 = 132 - x2 = 169 - 25 ⇒ AM2 = 144 ⇒ AM = 12

AB = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

questions.question: Find the least number divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18, which is a perfect square.
questions.questionHtml: Find the least number divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18, which is a perfect square.
questions.solution:
LCM (2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18) = 90

90 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 5.

As 2 and 5 are not in pair in LCM’s factor so we need to multiply 90 by 5 and 2 to make it a perfect square.

90 x 2 x 5  = 900.

questions.question: If \(\rm\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)\) = 2√2, what is the value of \(\rm\left(x^{6}+\frac{1}{x^{6}}\right)\) ?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)\) = 2√2, what is the value of \(\rm\left(x^{6}+\frac{1}{x^{6}}\right)\)?
questions.solution:
x + 1/x = 2√2 ⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = (2√2)2 - 2 ⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 6

Cubing both side we get

⇒ (x2 + 1/x2)3 = 63 ⇒ x6 + 1/x6 + 3 (x2 × 1/x2) (x2 + 1/x2)  = 63 ⇒ x6 + 1/x6 = 63 - 3 × 6 ⇒ x6 + 1/x6 = 198

54 + 63 =117 km/h = 117 * (5/18) = 65/2 m/s.

Time is taken by them to meet for the first time on the track while running in opposite direction = Length of track / relative speed in opposite direction

= 4225/(65/2) = 130 seconds

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters in the voter list did not cast their vote, whereas 10% of the votes cast were found to be invalid. The winning candidate got 56% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1,458 votes. What is the total number of voters enrolled in the voter list?
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters in the voter list did not cast their vote, whereas 10% of the votes cast were found to be invalid. The winning candidate got 56% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1,458 votes. What is the total number of voters enrolled in the voter list?
questions.solution:
Let, the total enrolled voters be x

valid vote = (90/100) × (9x/10) ⇒ 81x/100

The winning candidate got 56% of the polled vote means the looser got (100 – 56) = 44% vote

{(56/100) × (81x/100)} - {(44/100) × (81x/100)} = 1458 ⇒ (81x/100) × {(56 – 44)/100} = 1458 ⇒ (81 × 12)x/10000 = 1458 ⇒ x = (1458× 10000)/(81 × 12) ⇒ x = 15000

questions.question: The length, breadth, and height of a room are 10 m, 8 m and 6 m respectively. Find the cost of white washing the walls of the room and the ceiling at the rate of Rs. 7.50 per m 2 .
questions.questionHtml: The length, breadth, and height of a room are 10 m, 8 m and 6 m respectively. Find the cost of white washing the walls of the room and the ceiling at the rate of Rs. 7.50 per m<sup>2</sup>.
questions.solution:
Area of four walls of room = 2h (l + b)  = 2 × 6 (10 + 8) ⇒ 12 × 18= 216 m2

Area of ceiling = l × b = 10 × 8 = 80 m2

Total area of four walls and ceiling = 216 + 80 = 296 m2

Now, the cost of whitewashing the walls and ceiling = 296 × 7.50 = Rs.2,220

questions.question: Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The so-called harmless activities of a small number of people are increasingly becoming a serious problem for the internet. B. You would have seen an increasing amount of 'junk mail' showing up in your email box. C. It is basically electronic junk mail or junk newsgroup postings. D. Spam is the flooding of the internet with many copies of the same message, in an attempt to force the message on people who would not otherwise choose to receive it.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The so-called harmless activities of a small number of people are increasingly becoming a serious problem for the internet.

B. You would have seen an increasing amount of 'junk mail' showing up in your email box.

C. It is basically electronic junk mail or junk newsgroup postings.

D. Spam is the flooding of the internet with many copies of the same message, in an attempt to force the message on people who would not otherwise choose to receive it.
questions.solution: Sentence D begins with a definition and explanation of what spam is, setting the stage for the topic. Sentence A broadens the perspective by stating that the seemingly harmless activities of a small number of people are becoming a serious problem for the internet, tying back to the initial explanation of spam. Sentence B engages the reader by asking a question about their personal experience with spam, specifically mentioning 'junk mail' in email boxes. Sentence C is following the introduction and personal connection. So, the correct sequence is DABC.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The girl in the water whistled with full might and waved my arms to draw attention to her plight.
questions.questionHtml:

The girl in the water whistled with full might and waved my arms to draw attention to her plight.
questions.solution: The error in the sentence is a pronoun mismatch. In the original sentence, it says, "waved my arms," which suggests that the narrator (the person speaking or writing) is waving their own arms. However, considering the context, it is more likely that the girl in the water is the one waving her arms. Therefore, the pronoun "her" should be used to correctly refer to the girl in the water. Correct sentence: The girl in the water whistled with full might and waved her arms to draw attention to her plight.

questions.solution: The error lies in the use of the word "save." The error in the sentence is the use of "save" instead of "saved." Abraham Lincoln played a crucial role in preserving the Union during that conflict, and "saved" is the past tense form of the verb "save." The word "during" is used to indicate the time frame in which an action occurred. In this case, "during" is appropriate because it specifies the period when Abraham Lincoln saved the Union—namely, the time of the American Civil War. Correct sentence: Abraham Lincoln has been the sixteenth president of the United States and saved the Union during the American Civil War.
